newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nutricia profits soar, growth strong.
newsitem.headline: Nutricia profits soar, growth strong.

text.p: Dutch food group Nutricia on Thursday reported soaring 1996 profits and forecast that its earnings growth would continue to be strong in the current year.

Nutricia's 1996 net profits surged 52.6 percent to 232 million guilders ($122.7 million), in line with analysts' expectations, with operating profits soaring 62.2 percent to 340 million guilders, the company said in a statement.

The company announced a five for one share split, which will lower the nominal value per share from 2.50 to 0.50 guilders, and announced it was changing the name of the business to Numico in order to separate the firm's name from that of its brands.
Further efficiency and integration measures would continue to advance profit growth in 1997, Nutricia said.
"Combined with expected market developments, the results in the current financial year will show a substantial rise, barring unforseen circumstances," it said in a statement.
The figures came after the close of the Amsterdam bourse. Nutricia shares had finished up 10.00 guilders at 290.00.
"The results were in line with our expectations and there didn't seem to be any big surprises at this early stage," said analyst John David Roeg of Bank Labouchere.

Analysts had expected the continuing integration of the Milupa baby food business acquired in 1995 to again prove the main engine of growth and Nutricia said its German unit had contributed roughly 83 million guilders to the operating profit.
The company said that, excluding the effect of the Milupa takeover, autonomous growth had reached 7.1 percent in 1996.
"That's very positive," said ING Barings analyst Gerard Rijk. "It shows an acceleration even on the very strong growth we saw in the first half."
He said Nutricia was perhaps being slightly cautious in its predictions for profit growth in 1997.
In the language used by Dutch companies in results releases, "substantial rise" is often taken to denote an expected increase of between 12 and 20 percent.
"I expect 20 percent, but perhaps they are just being a little conservative," Rijk said.
Nutricia's earnings per share increased by nearly 40 percent to 9.58 guilders per share and the dividend was increased to 3.20 guilders from 2.10.
